Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the chase. The umpires and the players are out in the middle. Pathum Nissanka and Kusal Perera will be the openers for Sri Lanka. Shaheen Afridi comes to bowl. Let's play...
... The Run Chase ...

Right then, Pakistan have posted a good total of 252 runs on the board in this rain-curtailed game of 42 overs. They will be hoping for their bowlers to defend this. For Sri Lanka, the onus is on their batters to put up a gritty stand and chase this down. Which side will make it into the Asia Cup 2023 final? We shall find out soon. Chase coming up shortly...

Sri Lanka will be disappointed that they let it slip from a strong position with the ball. They failed to take full advantage of these overcast conditions. After Mohammad Nawaz's wickets, there was a short rain break, and once they got back in, they failed to pick up wickets. They did that at the very end but the damage was already done. Matheesha Pathirana picked up three wickets but was a bit expensive. Pramod Madushan chipped in with two wickets whilst Dunith Wellalage and Maheesh Theekshana picked up one wicket each and were the most economical of all.

So after the DLS adjustment, a run has been taken off Sri Lanka's target. So Sri Lanka's target now will be 252 runs in 42 overs. Pakistan have posted a total of 252 runs courtesy of some good batting from Mohammad Rizwan and Iftikhar Ahmed at the later part of the game. Let me remind you that Pakistan were reeling on 130/5 inside 28 overs. They were off to a shaky start but Rizwan-Iftikhar stitched up a partnership of 108 runs and made their side reach to a commendable total on this bowling paradise. Iftikhar Ahmed was dismissed at the very end for just three runs shy of his half-century. Mohammad Rizwan scored an unbeaten 86 runs for his side.

FOUR! Wow! Just wow! What a shot that is. That was by no means a bad ball but Mohammad Rizwan has timed it so well. A boundary to end the innings. A yorker outside off, this is jammed through point. Two fielders in the deep but it bisects them to find the gap. PAKISTAN END WITH 252!

OUT! STUMPED! That's a jaffa and some swift glovework by Kusal Mendis has done the job! Dunith Wellalage continues to build his reputation as a legend killer. He hunted down some superstars from India in the last game and now he has removed the number one ODI batter in Babar Azam. This is some smart thinking from the young man. A couple of deliveries drift down the leg side and this time, Dunith flights a full ball around off and gets it to spin away from the batter. Babar Azam leans forward to block it but gets beaten. Kusal Mendis grabs the ball and whips off the bails in a flash. The umpire goes upstairs to have a check. No outside edge is found. The replay shows that Babar Azam's back leg was in the air when the bails were off and he has to depart. The partnership is finally broken and Dunith Wellalage is getting mobbed by his teammates.

Commentary.Commentary: We are all set to play. The players and the umpires are out in the middle followed by the Pakistan openers - Fakhar Zaman and Abdullah Shafique. Pramod Madushan will start the proceedings with the new ball. Let's go...

Dasun Shanaka the skipper of Sri Lanka says they would have bowled with the weather Around and the wicket might take a turn. Adds it didn't turn a lot in the evening and that's why they want to chase. Ends by saying they have a few changes too.

Babar Azam the skiper of Pakistan says they want to put runs on the board and the pitch might play a little differently later on. Informs Imam is out and Fakhar is back in and there are a few more changes.

Sri Lanka (Playing XI) - Pathum Nissanka, Kusal Perera (In for Dimuth Karunaratne), Kusal Mendis (WK), Sadeera Samarawickrama, Charith Asalanka, Dhananjaya de Silva, Dasun Shanaka (C), Dunith Wellalage, Maheesh Theekshana, Pramod Madushan (In for Kasun Rajitha), Matheesha Pathirana.

Pakistan (Playing XI) - Fakhar Zaman, Abdullah Shafique (In for Imam-ul-Haq), Babar Azam (C), Mohammad Rizwan (WK), Mohammad Haris (In for Agha Salman), Iftikhar Ahmed, Shadab Khan, Mohammad Nawaz (In for Faheem Ashraf), Shaheen Afridi, Mohammad Wasim (In for Haris Rauf), Zaman Khan (In for Naseem Shah).
TOSS - Pakistan have won the toss and will BAT first.

Update 4.43 pm IST (11.13 am GMT) - Most of the covers are off now and the rain has stopped completely. The toss will take place at 5 pm IST (11.30 am GMT) and the game will begin at 5.15 pm IST (11.45 am GMT). It will be a 45 overs per-side game.

Update 4.02 pm IST (10.32 am GMT) - The rain seems to have eased off a bit now and the groundsmen are trying to get the water off the covers. Let's hope it stays this way and we get some cricketing action soon. The cut-off time for a 20-over game is 9.02 pm IST, and we will begin to lose overs from 4.30 pm IST.

Update 3.25 pm IST (9.55 am GMT) - The rain has got a bit heavier now at the R.Premadasa Stadium, Colombo and the entire ground is covered again. It has got a bit dark too which is not a good sign. The waiting game continues for now.

Update 3.01 pm IST (9.31 am GMT) - Sigh! Both the captains were almost in the middle for the toss but it started to rain again and it forced the players to go back into the dressing room. Let's hope it is just a passing shower and the game begins soon. Stay tuned for more updates.

Update 2.40 pm IST (9.10 am GMT) - Some good news! It has stopped raining here and covers are slowly coming off. If it stays this way, the toss will take place at 2.50 pm IST (9.20 am GMT) and the game will begin at 3.15 pm IST (9.45 am GMT). The Pakistan players are seen in a huddle and Zaman Khan receives his debut ODI cap.

Update 2.21 pm IST (8.51 am GMT) - Well, there is a bit of rain in the air at the moment. Not that heavy though but the entire ground is under covers and the TOSS HAS BEEN DELAYED. Stick around for regular updates...

On the flip side, the injuries have been a concern for Pakistan's side. They lost the last game against their arch-rivals by a mammoth margin of 228 runs. They will look to leave that behind and bounce back into this game. They have announced their Playing XI and come into this game with five changes. Mohammad Haris, Saud Shakeel, Mohammad Nawaz, Mohammad Wasim, and Zaman Khan come in for Fakhar Zaman, Agha Salman, Faheem Ashraf, Haris Rauf, and Naseem Shah. So, who will be the second finalists of this Asia Cup? We shall find out soon. Stay tuned for toss and other updates.

So, we are on to the fifth and the do-or-die game of the Super Four as Pakistan goes against Sri Lanka. The Lankans have been brilliant under the leadership of Dasun Shanaka. They lost a close game against India in their previous encounter but the positive for them is that the youngster Dunith Wellalage showed his worth. Their bowling unit has been excellent so far and they will be overall happy with their performances. They will look to win this one and make their way again into the finals of the Asia Cup.

The quest to make way into the finals of the Asia Cup 2023 and the only question in everyone's mind is WHO WILL IT BE? India have well booked their spot in the finals and are the only team who are yet to face a defeat in Asia Cup 2023. For Sri Lanka and Pakistan, this is the final fixture and the winner of this game will make it to the grand finale against the Indians. The weather gods though are not in our favor but let's hope we have a rain-free game today...
... MATCH TIME ...

We are all set for the 5th match in the Super 4 stages of the Asia Cup 2023. The venue for the game is the capital city of Sri Lanka, Colombo where the co-hosts, Sri Lanka and Pakistan will face off against each other. Both teams are coming into this match after facing a loss against India. This is a crucial match for both teams as the qualification in the finals will depend on this match. Pakistan have had a very hectic schedule in this tournament due to a lot of travelling due to the hybrid mode. However, they will have had a good 2 days rest before this match. They have a lot of things to discuss about as their performance in the last game was very disappointing. They missed a trick by not having any proper spinner in their team against the game in India. Their pace attack also faced a huge blow with the possible injury of Haris Rauf and Naseem Shah in the end. Agha Salman was also bruised in their last match after he got hit by the ball under his right eye. The fitness of all of them will be a topic of concern as this is a critical stage in the tournament. Their pace attack was shattered in their last match as they leaked many runs. After the poor performance of their bowling attack, the batters too couldn't stand up to the challenge as their top order crumbled under pressure. The middle order fell to the spinning magic weaved by the opposition. The trouble their batters faced against the spinners will increase more against Sri Lanka as the pitch has shown a good amount of turn in recent matches. The only positive for Pakistan was the economical bowling by Naseem Shah but he too had to undergo checks for a possible injury. Sri Lanka, on the other hand, had a good outing for their bowling unit against the Indians. The youngster, Dunith Wellalage, was the man of the match for his fifer which helped restrict their opposition to a relatively low total. He along with Maheesh will lead the spin attack. This team had been battered by injuries of their main players right before this tournament but, they have performed really well throughout with a squad of youngsters. The slinger, Matheesha Pathirana is brilliant in the death overs which is a big positive for them. Their batting unit, however, did not perform as expected in the last match as they failed to chase the target, losing by 41 runs. Dhananjaya de Silva and Dunith Wellalage were the only batters to cross the 25-run mark but the rest of them couldn't get as many runs. This will be a big concern against the lethal pace attack of Pakistan. This will surely be an interesting match to watch. Will Sri Lanka make use of their home conditions or will the second-best ODI team bounce back strongly? We will find out soon.
